title: The Peacegiver: How Christ Offers to Heal Our Hearts and Homes
author: James L. Ferrell
target_audience: Christians seeking personal or family peace
Individuals struggling with resentment or conflict
Readers interested in gospel-centered healing and forgiveness
Any person looking for practical application of Christian teachings in relationships
core_themes: Personal application of the Atonement of Jesus Christ
Applying scriptural teachings to real-life challenges
primary_purpose: To teach readers how Jesus Christ’s atonement can practically and deeply transform one’s heart, heal wounded relationships, and bring genuine inner peace, using parable, scripture, and personal narrative as applied to everyday family and marital challenges.

structure_format.organization: Primarily a modern parable with interwoven scriptural analysis and real-life application; alternates between the protagonist’s personal struggles and hypothetical/scriptural conversations
features: Frequent references to the Bible and Book of Mormon
Reflection questions and moments of self-examination

key_concepts_lessons: True peace and healing come only through Jesus Christ’s atonement.
Forgiveness is attainable even when one feels deeply wronged.
Resentment and anger often stem from pride and misunderstandings.
Scriptural stories illustrate real principles that can be directly applied to modern conflicts.
Changing one’s perspective can transform relationships, especially in marriage and family.
Personal responsibility, rather than blaming others, brings spiritual growth and healing.
notable_features: Tells a fictional narrative to teach gospel principles
Focus on practical application of scriptural stories (e.g., Jonah, Abigail and David)
Particularly addresses marital and family discord
Written from an LDS perspective but broadly applicable to other Christians
cultural_historical_context: Published during a period of renewed emphasis in the LDS Church and broader Christian circles on applying the Atonement to everyday living, particularly addressing emotional struggles and family dynamics in the early 21st century.
reception_impact: Highly regarded among Latter-day Saint audiences
Frequently recommended in marriage, family, and faith-based counseling
Praised for its relatable storytelling and accessible spiritual insights
Some critics note its LDS-specific doctrinal elements may limit universal appeal
comparable_titles: The Gift of Forgiveness by Philip Yancey
Believing Christ by Stephen E. Robinson
The Bonds That Make Us Free by C. Terry Warner
